record.original_question: In fixed-budget best arm identification, a bandit instance mu belongs to the class S of instances with a unique best arm, the learner uses exactly n samples, and then outputs an estimate I_hat_n of the best arm; the resulting error probability is p_{mu,n} = P_mu(I_hat_n != I*(mu)), where I*(mu) is the unique arm with the largest mean. Is there a natural algorithm class A and a well-defined instance-dependent function Gamma*_fb: S -> R such that every algorithm in A satisfies lim inf_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) >= Gamma*_fb(mu), while some algorithm in A also satisfies the matching upper bound lim sup_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) <= Gamma*_fb(mu), so that Gamma*_fb exactly characterizes the asymptotic complexity of the fixed-budget setting?

evidence.quote: In the fixed-budget setting, a budget of n samples is fixed and given. After collecting n samples, the experimenter needs to decide an estimate of the identity of the best arm denoted by I_hat_n. An algorithm is then only consists of a sampling rule and a decision rule. The experimenter's objective in the fixed-budget setting is to minimize the probability of incorrect decision defined as p_{mu,n} = P_mu(I_hat_n != I*(mu)).

Open problem 1. The first and foremost open problem is whether there are a desirable algorithm class A and a well-defined function Gamma*_fb : S -> R such that for any algorithm in A, for all mu in S, lim inf_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) >= Gamma*_fb(mu) and there is an algorithm that belongs to A and guarantees for all mu in S, lim sup_{n->infinity} n / log(1/p_{mu,n}) <= Gamma*_fb(mu).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the stochastic multi-armed bandit problem with finitely many arms. A bandit instance $\mu = (\mu_1, \ldots, \mu_K)$ specifies the distribution of each arm; let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the class of instances admitting a unique best arm, i.e. a unique index $I^*(\mu) \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ whose mean reward is strictly larger than that of every other arm.

In the fixed-budget best-arm identification problem, a total number of samples $n$ is fixed in advance. An algorithm consists of (i) a sampling rule that at each round $t = 1, \ldots, n$ chooses an arm $A_t$ as a (possibly randomized) function of past observations, and (ii) a decision rule that, after observing all $n$ samples, outputs a guess $\hat{I}_n \in \{1, \ldots, K\}$ for the identity of the best arm. The error probability of the algorithm on instance $\mu$ with budget $n$ is
$$p_{\mu,n} := \mathbb{P}_\mu\bigl(\hat{I}_n \neq I^*(\mu)\bigr).$$

Question: Do there exist a class $\mathcal{A}$ of admissible algorithms and an instance-dependent function $\Gamma^*_{\mathrm{fb}} : \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item (lower bound) for every algorithm in $\mathcal{A}$ and every $\mu \in \mathcal{S}$,
$$\liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{n}{\log(1/p_{\mu,n})} \;\geq\; \Gamma^*_{\mathrm{fb}}(\mu),$$
\item (matching upper bound) there exists an algorithm in $\mathcal{A}$ such that for every $\mu \in \mathcal{S}$,
$$\limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{n}{\log(1/p_{\mu,n})} \;\leq\; \Gamma^*_{\mathrm{fb}}(\mu),$$
\end{enumerate}
so that $\Gamma^*_{\mathrm{fb}}(\mu)$ exactly characterizes the asymptotic complexity of fixed-budget best-arm identification on $\mathcal{S}$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the well-known fixed-budget best-arm identification complexity problem posed by Qin (2022). Subsequent works (e.g., Degenne 2023 on the large-deviation perspective, and a 2026 reduction showing "fixed budget is no harder than fixed confidence up to logarithmic factors") have produced partial results, improved bounds, and structural connections to the fixed-confidence setting, but no work has provided a fully matching instance-dependent characterization $\Gamma^*_{\mathrm{fb}}$ together with a suitable algorithm class. The problem is widely cited as still open.

status_evidence.title: Best Arm Identification with Fixed Budget: A Large Deviation Perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizing the minimal instance-specific error probability for this problem constitutes one of the important remaining open problems in MABs.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work explicitly states the instance-specific complexity remains an important open problem.

status_evidence.title: Fixed Budget is No Harder Than Fixed Confidence in Best-Arm Identification up to Logarithmic Factors
status_evidence.snippet: FB is no harder than FC up to logarithmic factors.
status_evidence.claim: Only logarithmic-factor relations are known; no exact matching constant has been established.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Optimal Best Arm Identification with Fixed Budget
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem statement by Qin on existence of an algorithm class and Gamma*_fb characterizing fixed-budget asymptotic complexity.
status_evidence.claim: Original formulation of the open problem.
